rules.numbers: knot tangent = mean of the two adjacent secants, then clamped to 3x the secant so the curve can never overshoot or reverse (fusion_motion.curve). settle() prepends a 2-frame step covering 12% of the travel so the move starts from rest, not from the cable. Seam velocity = mean(enter secant, drift secant): card 0.93->1.00 in 16 f (0.44%/f) then 1.00->1.085 over the remaining 44 f of a 60-f beat (0.19%/f) -> 0.31%/f at the moment of arrival = 1.4 px/f at 1080. Never 0.
rules.rule: Entrance and drift are ONE monotone cubic spline (Fritsch-Carlson); the velocity at the arrival knot is never zero — that is the whole difference from 'entered then stopped'.

rules.numbers: measured travel, all beats: wordmark +8 px width over 5 frames (+1.0%); reel-02 logo-swap left edge 290->270 px over 9 f (20 px = 1.0% of W); biggest travel anywhere = 116 px = 6.0% of H (a file literally dropping); typical plate travel 20-40 px = 1-2% of H. Nothing travels >1/3 of the frame (skill 1/3 Rule holds).
rules.rule: Nothing flies in from off-frame. The reference cuts into an almost-final layout and lets the settle + shine + drift carry the motion. Travel is a settle, not a flight.
rules.source: measured on video/projects/000-video-to-copy/source/reel-01/02-Dd*.mp4, 30 fps, frames extracted with ffmpeg

rules.numbers: enter_frames 16, enter_size 0.93, rise 0.016 (= 30.7 px at 1920), zoom_to 1.085, pan_x 0.012 (= +-13.0 px at 1080), alternate direction per take, motion blur on with shutter 270 / quality 4.
rules.rule: Entrance amplitude for a card/plate: scale 0.93 -> 1.00 plus a rise of 0.016 of frame height, over 16 frames.

rules.numbers: chip enter_frames 12, rise 0.022 (= 42.2 px at 1920), size curve 0.97->1.00->1.00, fade Blend = f/12 sampled per frame (linear, on purpose: the transform is splined, the fade is linear). Chip plate padding [0.04, 0.03] of canvas, plate alpha 0.92 (title) / 1.0 (gold CTA), radius_pt 20.
rules.rule: Entrance amplitude for a chip/pill: smaller and quicker than a plate — scale 0.97 -> 1.00, rise 0.022, 12 frames, with a LINEAR opacity fade 0->1 across those same 12 frames.

rules.numbers: reel-02 b05 logo swap left edge 290 -> 276 -> 272 -> 270 at frames 218/221/224/227 = 0.70 / 0.90 / 1.00 of the travel (settled in 9 f). reel-01 b04 card bottom edge 622 -> 686 in ONE frame, then 686 -> 699 over the next 5 (f234-240). reel-01 b01 wordmark 840 -> 843 -> 845 -> 847 -> 848 px at frames 1-5.
rules.rule: Measured entrance profile in the reference is a hard ease-out: ~70% of the travel lands in the first 3 frames, the last 30% takes another 5-6.

rules.numbers: micro-feedback 3-6 f / chip, pill 12 f / plate, card, b-roll 16 f / hero logo, number, wordmark 20-24 f (measured: reel-02 big block bbox grew 484 -> 529 px = +9.3% over 12-16 f). Fade components stay linear; every transform is splined.
rules.rule: Duration ladder by element size (30 fps). Bigger element = longer entrance; distances do not share a duration.

rules.numbers: measured sustained drift: 0.35 px/f on a progress-bar cap (14 px over 40 f), 0.17 px/f on the reel-02 logo block, 0.03 px/f on the persistent wordmark. Budget 0.3-0.6 px/f at 1080 = 18-36 px over a 2 s beat. Preset version of the same idea: keep growing zoom to 1.085 while panning +-12.96 px, sign alternating per take; grid/background layer moves at 0.2x of that (pan_x 0.010, zoom 0.05).
rules.rule: After the entrance the object keeps drifting — small, monotone, forever. Never a still frame on a B/C canvas.

rules.numbers: measured on the ANTHROPIC wordmark (reel-01 b01, 81 f long): first brightening at frame 7 (0.23 s into the beat), peak crosses bucket 1 at f9, last bucket at f17, gone by f19 -> 13 frames total = 0.43 s. Travel ~984 px (844 px mark + band) at 76-88 px/f with a short ease-out in the last 2 frames. No second sweep.
rules.rule: Shine sweep: LEFT -> RIGHT across the mark, once, starting ~7 frames after the cut.
rules.source: measured, per-frame glyph-band luminance on source/reel-01-DdL6K53lWEm.mp4 frames 1-49

rules.numbers: glyph pixels (mask of the mark's own alpha) go from luminance ~35 to a peak of ~205-210 = +170, i.e. the stroke reads 13% -> 81% white at the crest. Band FWHM = 140 px (13% of frame width, 4 of 24 35-px buckets above half max); total soft footprint ~280 px. Outside the band the glyph returns to its base value on the very next frame — no residue.
rules.rule: The shine acts on the INK, not on an overlay: it lifts the glyph fill toward white while the silhouette stays put.

rules.numbers: frames 23-32 (10 f, ~0.35 s after the sweep ends): every bucket rises together by +15-20 luminance (peak at f25-26) with a simultaneous scale breath 848 -> 854 -> 844 px (0.0 -> +0.7% -> -0.5%), then settles back to the 848 baseline. One soft event per beat; a second travelling sweep is not in the reference.
rules.rule: A soft uniform halo breath follows the shine — the mark is never left static after the sweep.

rules.numbers: pill height 94 px (4.9% of 1920), width 179-198 px, clear gap between siblings 14 px, pill row centre y = 1222 (63.6% of H); the row's bbox grew 371 -> 391 px wide and 94 -> 113 -> 94 px high during a 20-f settle. List-plate in reel-01 b04: 190-207 px wide x ~337 px tall, centred at x = 537 (dead centre).
rules.rule: Chip / pill geometry from the reference product-UI canvas.
rules.source: measured, reel-02 b03 frames 74-110 and reel-01 b04 frames 230-320

rules.numbers: reel-01 b04 swaps at frames 234 / 259-260 / 289-290 -> 25 and 30 frames per item (0.83-1.0 s), matching the spoken clause, not a musical grid. New item arrives at ~0.90 of final and expands to full over 6-9 f (y-extent 495 -> 607 -> 623 -> 632 -> 698 across f291-297). Frame-to-frame delta inside a held item is 0.0 for up to 30 consecutive frames.
rules.rule: List / item swap is a HARD CUT on the item, not a crossfade and not a slide; the new item then settles in 6-9 frames.

rules.numbers: measured 'Installing 0->100%' (reel-01 b10, cut at f754): first pixel at f769 (15 f = 0.5 s after the cut), then 0.4% at f771, 10.5% f775, 32.3% f780, 52.3% f784, 75.1% f790, 91.4% f798, 99.4% f810 -> 0 to 99% in 40 frames = 1.33 s. Velocity per frame rises 1.9 -> 5.1 (peak at ~45% fill, 2.5x the mean) then falls to 0.2. Track 474 px wide (43.9% of W), x 303..777 (centred), row y = 848 (44% of H). The cap's left edge also drifts +14 px right over the 40 f (0.35 px/f).
rules.rule: A bar/percentage fills as an EASE-IN-OUT, not a linear ramp: it accelerates out of 0 and decelerates into the value.
rules.source: measured, per-frame run-length scan, reel-01 b10 frames 752-815

rules.numbers: reel-01 b04 f250 ink bands: y 272-408 (h = 137, the hero) / y 454-495 (h = 42, label) / y 536-634 (h = 99). Hero:label ratio ~3:1. Exactly one shine per beat; exactly one element drifts above 0.5 px/f.
rules.rule: One hero per frame. Rank by ink mass; the hero gets the entrance, the drift and the shine — support gets none of them.
rules.source: measured row/column ink profiling + PATTERNS.md motion hierarchy

rules.numbers: full-frame scale search over 0.96-1.05 preferred 1.000 in every beat pair measured (no punch, no zoom per beat); host-band motion |dx|,|dy| <= 2 px in 26 of 32 pairs (that is the person, not the edit); a settled card held x 442..632 with a frame-to-frame delta of 0.0 for 30 consecutive frames — only the shine moved over it. No rotation anywhere. Intensity comes from the palco change, never from a camera punch.
rules.rule: What is deliberately NOT animated: the camera, the frame, the page background, the host, and text that has already settled.
rules.source: measured (best_shift / best_scale over all 32+36 beat pairs) + PATTERNS.md 'Intensidade = troca de palco, não punch de câmera'

rules.numbers: reference wordmark 844 x 94 px, x 118..961 = 78% of frame width, cap height 94 px (4.9% of H), centred at x = 539. Palco B split line at 50.0% (reel-01) / 52.9% (reel-02, strongest horizontal edge at y = 1016); host card corner radius documented 80-120 px, measured arc R ~= 200 px on the top-left corner. Our palco B graphic band y 40..700 (660 px): hero mark/plate <= 840 px wide, centred x = 540 -> x 120..960, cap height 88-96 px. Stacked chips (h 96 + gap 20): 3 chips = 328 px, fits the 660 px band with air left for the drift.
rules.rule: Frame geometry to build against (reference measurements translated to our 1080x1920).
rules.source: measured + PATTERNS.md 'Medidas observadas' (split, raio ~80-120 px) + MOTION-BRIEF technical table

rules.numbers: two shadow layers, never one: contact = blur 7 px, offset y -0.004 (-7.7 px), opacity 0.5, scale 1.0; ambient = blur 42 px, offset y -0.02 (-38.4 px), opacity 0.34, scale 1.008. Corner radius = radius_pt 20 x canvas_w / (1080 x zoom), so a card shown at 50% still shows a 20 pt corner. Motion blur shutter 270, quality 4 on EVERY animated transform.
rules.rule: Shadows and corners are sized in reference units, not in pixels of the current card, so they read the same at any size.

rules.numbers: graphic drift 0.3-0.6 px/f while caption words cut every 8-15 f. No whoosh per cut; no music bed by default. SFX only as a motivated event (snap at a chip landing, riser on a bar fill), tempo local to the clip.
rules.rule: The graphic must move slower than the caption changes; the graphic carries the continuous layer, the cut carries the punctuation.
rules.source: PATTERNS.md Som + FORMULAS/BEHAVIORS.md 'Canvas B/C sempre em motion' + MOTION-BRIEF sfx-cues

enter_recipes.desc: Per chip: size knots [(0, 0.97), (12, 1.00), (L, 1.00)] and center knots [(0, y+42px), (12, y), (L, y)] fed through settle() (2-frame pre-step at 12% of travel), then a monotone spline sampled every frame so the chip is still moving 0.5-1 px/f when it lands. Opacity is LINEAR 0->1 over the first 12 frames (do not ease the fade). Stagger 4 frames per chip, top-to-bottom; allow a 1.5-3% scale overshoot on the chips only (measured reference return ~11% on a 95 px travel). A 3-chip stack therefore finishes at frame 12+8 = 20, which fits u01 (57 f) and u07 (36 f) with room for the drift. Motion blur on, shutter 270/quality 4.
enter_recipes.name: chip_enter (u01, u07, u12)

enter_recipes.desc: size [(0, 0.93), (16, 1.00), (L, 1.085)], center [(0, y+31px), (16, y), (L, y - 6px)], pan_x 0.012 x direction (-1 or +1, alternate per beat). One spline, sampled frame by frame into the transform; the 1.085 tail is the drift, so the plate is still creeping when the beat cuts. Fade linear 0->1 over 12 f. Shadow: contact 7 px / -7.7 px / 0.5 plus ambient 42 px / -38 px / 0.34. For palco B, cull every pixel below y=960 at render time and clamp shadow blur so it never crosses y=700.
enter_recipes.name: plate_enter (u09, u10, u11 cards; b-roll plates)

enter_recipes.desc: Measured shape: the mark arrives at 99% and settles the last 1% — size [(0, 0.99), (5, 1.00)] then a breath to 1.007 at ~frame 25 and back to 1.0, i.e. knots [(0,0.99),(5,1.00),(24,1.007),(34,0.995),(48,1.00)]. Position travel <= 20 px. For a big block entering cold (u05, 75 f) use the heavier version: [(0, 0.92), (16, 1.00), (75, 1.085)] with a 30 px rise. Hero mark width <= 840 px at 1080, centred x=540.
enter_recipes.name: hero_enter (u04 JEV mark, u05 ChatGPT logo, u13 number)

enter_recipes.desc: Hard cut on the item at the clause boundary — no crossfade, no slide. The incoming card is drawn at 0.90 for exactly 1 frame then expands to 1.00 over 6-9 frames (measured y-extent 495 -> 607 -> 623 -> 632 -> 698, frames 291-297), while the outgoing card is simply gone. Cadence 25-30 frames per item (the spoken clause, ~0.9 s), NOT a metronome. Keep the palco identical across the chain; only the plate changes.
enter_recipes.name: swap_item (u09/u10/u11 card chain, P9/P14)

enter_recipes.desc: Knots [(0, 0), (20, 0.45), (40, 0.99)] through the monotone spline = ease-in-out with the velocity peak (5.1%/frame) at the 45% mark and 0 at both ends. 40 frames for 0->99% (measured 1.33 s), first pixel 15 frames after the cut. Track 474 px wide (43.9% of W) centred at x=540, drawn as a 6 px-tall rounded cap of the fill colour (gold #F4B400 for the winner, muted #5A544E for the losers). The cap's left edge also creeps +0.35 px/frame so the bar never freezes. The % label counts up on the same 40-frame spline, no separate easing.
enter_recipes.name: bar_fill (u01 % bars, u03 probability, u08)

enter_recipes.desc: 5 enters at frame 0 with hero_enter; 18 replaces it at ~frame 60 with a 1-frame swap + 8-frame settle; the x locks at ~frame 100 and then must keep drifting (0.2-0.4 px/f so a 6.3 s beat never stalls). One shine is allowed on the x, starting ~frame 100, width 140 px FWHM, 13 frames; one halo breath around frame 140. No second travelling shine. The small ChatGPT logo enters on support timing (16 f) and stays under 30% of the hero's ink mass.
enter_recipes.name: number_lock (u13 5-18x, 190 frames)

enter_recipes.desc: Digits step down on a 6-frame grid (0,50 -> 0,49 -> ... ) with each digit pair changing by a 1-frame swap plus a 3-frame settle, never a smooth tween (a real timer snaps). The final 0,50 lands ~12 frames before the beat end so it holds and drifts; a riser marks the lock. Keep every glyph the same pixel height so the number does not jitter width — use tabular figures from Hetrixo.
enter_recipes.name: timer_tick (u14, 0,50 s, 57 frames)

enter_recipes.desc: One travelling band, left -> right, over the mark's own alpha only (mask the logo asset, sweep inside the mask, never paint outside it). Start 7 frames after the cut, 13 frames long, band FWHM 140 px (13% of W) with soft ramps (~280 px footprint), near-linear travel at 76-88 px/f with an ease-out in the last 2 frames, ink luminance 35 -> 205 (+170) at the crest. Then a 10-frame uniform halo breath (+15-20 luminance) starting ~4 frames after the sweep ends. If the beat is shorter than 40 frames, compress to: start frame 4, 9 frames, band FWHM 110 px — never stretch the entrance instead.
enter_recipes.name: logo_shine (u04, u05, u12)

shine: Measured on the ANTHROPIC wordmark (reel-01 beat 1, 81 frames): the sweep starts at frame 7 (0.23 s after the cut), travels LEFT -> RIGHT, and is gone by frame 19 — 13 frames total, 0.43 s. It is a single band, not a loop: band FWHM 140 px (13% of frame width, ~4 of 24 35-px buckets above half max), total soft footprint ~280 px, moving at 76-88 px/frame (near-linear, with a short ease-out over the last 2 frames). It acts on the ink, not on the canvas: masked to the mark's own alpha, the glyph fill luminance goes from ~35 to ~205-210 at the crest (+170, i.e. the stroke reads 13% -> 81% white) and returns to base on the next frame with no residue — the silhouette never moves. Exactly one sweep per beat. Four frames after it ends, a uniform halo breath (frames 23-32, 10 frames, +15-20 luminance across every bucket, simultaneous with a 848 -> 854 -> 844 px scale breath) so the mark is never left static after the sweep — this is the second soft event, not a second sweep. For our short beats (u04 = 32 f, u12 = 56 f) use the compressed variant: start frame 4, 9 frames long, band FWHM 110 px, halo 6 frames. Mask the shine to the band y 40..700 on palco B so the sweep never reaches the caption band.
chips: Reference product-UI canvas: pill height 94 px (4.9% of 1920), width 179-198 px, clear gap between siblings 14 px, row centred on the vertical axis (reel-02 pills x 342..539 and 553..731, row centre y = 1222 = 63.6% of H; reel-01 list plates 190-207 px wide, ~337 px tall, centred at x = 537). Entry: first chip is on screen at the cut, the next one starts 5 frames later (measured f76 -> f81), then each chip settles on its own 12-frame spline — scale 0.97 -> 1.00 and a 42 px rise (0.022 of H), opacity LINEAR 0 -> 1 across those 12 frames, monotone spline so the chip is still moving ~0.5-1 px/f when it lands. Stagger 4 frames top-to-bottom; a 3-chip stack completes at frame 20. Cap a group at 700 ms total (animation-principles) — with 4 chips use 3 frames of stagger, not 5. Rows stay put once settled (measured frame-to-frame delta 0.0 for 30 consecutive frames) except for the group's shared 0.3-0.6 px/f drift. When the row is a CHAIN of cards (u09/u10/u11), do not stagger — HARD CUT the item at the clause boundary and let the incoming plate expand 0.90 -> 1.00 over 6-9 frames, at 25-30 frames per item. Bar-style fills (u01 %s, u03 probability) are NOT chips: they fill ease-in-out over 40 frames, peak velocity 5.1%/frame at the 45% mark, starting 15 frames after the cut. On palco B keep the whole chip stack inside y 40..700 with the last chip's baseline no lower than y 660, and let the bottom 260 px of the canvas stay empty for the other agent's captions.
risks: Beat budget: 09-jev beats are much shorter than the reference's 2.0-2.7 s. u04 is 32 f and u07 is 36 f, but a 16-frame entrance plus a 13-frame shine plus a 7-frame shine offset = 36 f — the whole beat. Use the compressed variants (chip 12 f, shine start f4 / 9 f) and never stretch the entrance to fill the beat; if it still does not fit, cut the shine, not the drift.

Palco B is transparent with a hard floor at y=960 and a caption band at 700..960. The preset's ambient shadow (blur 42 px, offset -38 px) and any glow will bleed into 700..960 and past 960 — clamp/cull below y=700 and verify the alpha is 0 for every pixel below 960 (sample a PNG, as the brief demands). A 42 px blur centred at y=650 already reaches y=700.

Remotion has no Fritsch-Carlson built in. interpolate() with an easing option is NOT the same curve, and spring() overshoots by construction. Port curve()/settle() to TypeScript (10 lines of Hermite + the clamping loop) or every entrance will land with the exact 'entrou e parou' jerk the brief bans.

'Snappy with a short overshoot on chips' (brief) conflicts with the engine's monotone guarantee (never overshoots). Keep the conflict explicit: allow <=3% scale overshoot on chips and never on numbers, bars or logos — the reference shows an ~11% return on a 95 px travel, so a 3% budget is already conservative.

The reference is a talking-head Reel whose 'canvas' is a mock product UI at an unknown design scale. Its pixel numbers (94 px pill, 844 px wordmark) are measured in a 1080x1920 frame and transfer directly, but anything derived from the mascot illustration does not. Re-derive per beat against our fixed bands (y 40..700 palco B, y 80..1400 palco C) instead of scaling blindly.

u13 is 190 frames (6.33 s) — long enough that a monotone drift can read as frozen if the rate is below ~0.2 px/f. Budget one soft event mid-beat (a halo breath or a second number swap) and keep the x locked with a visible micro-drift; the measured reference halo breath (frames 23-32, +15-20 luminance) is the precedent.

Palco C is opaque cream and only 1320 px of graphic height is usable, with 1500..1750 reserved for captions. The hero number (5-18x) must not grow into the caption band — cap the number block height at ~460 px ending by y=1400.

The current edit/overlay/u*_B.png / u*_C.png and edit/render_canvas.py are the PIL raster with the scale-8-frames hack. They are useful for one thing only: confirming the alpha contract below y=960 on palco B. Do not port a single coordinate, timing or easing value from them.
